literalGroups.primaryGround: The prompt asks for the peace treaty ending the Russo-Japanese War. The official U.S. historical source identifies Portsmouth as formally ending that war; the San Stefano diplomatic record concerns peace between Russia and Turkey in 1878; the Library of Congress dates Versailles to 1919 and the WWI settlement; the Brest text concerns Russia and the Quadruple Alliance in 1918. The alternatives are parallel treaty names, but only Portsmouth matches the named Russo-Japanese conflict.

literalGroups.literal: Русско-японскую войну завершил Портсмутский мир 1905 года, заключённый при посредничестве президента США Теодора Рузвельта. Россия признала преобладающие интересы Японии в Корее и уступила южную часть Сахалина.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The official Office of the Historian account supports the Portsmouth treaty ending the Russo-Japanese War, its 1905 signature, Roosevelt’s brokerage role, Japan’s position in Korea and southern Sakhalin, and the absence of a Russian indemnity.

literalGroups.literal: Сан-Стефанский мир 1878 года завершил русско-турецкую войну.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The contemporary U.S. diplomatic dispatch records the Russia–Turkey peace preliminaries signed at San Stefano on 3 March 1878, calls the treaty the end of a war, and reproduces an English translation of the official treaty text. This distinguishes the 1878 Russo-Turkish peace from the 1905 Russo-Japanese settlement.

literalGroups.literal: Портсмутский мир не предусматривал выплаты Россией военной контрибуции Японии.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The official account says Russia refused an indemnity and that the treaty did not require Russia to pay Japan’s war costs. This is an additional treaty fact beyond the answer and explanation.

literalGroups.literal: Версальский договор 1919 года урегулировал отношения с Германией после Первой мировой войны.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Library of Congress identifies the 28 June 1919 Versailles Treaty as signed by Germany and the Allied Nations and as formally ending World War One, supporting the note’s distinction from the Russo-Japanese peace.

literalGroups.literal: Брестский мир 1918 года вывел Советскую Россию из Первой мировой войны.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Department of State’s published treaty text identifies Brest Litovsk and Article 1 declares the condition of war between Russia and the Quadruple Alliance powers ceased; it gives the signature date as 3 March 1918.
